```plato
    // The two bodies after one visit to a distance joint. `stiffness` is the
    // fraction of the length error removed per step, in [0, 1].
    //
    // The impulse's sign is clamped to match the violation: a joint that is too
    // long may only pull and a joint that is too short may only push. Without that
    // clamp a rope would hold its ends apart as well as together, which is a rod.
    SolveJoint(bodies: Array<SolverBody3D>, joint: DistanceJoint, stiffness: Number,
        seconds: Number): Array<SolverBody3D>
    {
        var a = bodies[joint.BodyA.Value];
        var b = bodies[joint.BodyB.Value];
        var anchorA = WorldAnchor(a, joint.AnchorA);
        var anchorB = WorldAnchor(b, joint.AnchorB);
        var span = anchorA.Between(anchorB);
        var separation = span.Magnitude;
        var axis = separation > 0.0 ? span / separation : Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
        var error = DistanceError(joint, separation);
        var raw = ImpulseFor(
            JointBias(error, stiffness, seconds),
            SeparationSpeed(a, b, anchorA, anchorB, axis),
            DirectionalMass(a, b, anchorA, anchorB, axis));
        // Too long: pull, so the impulse on B must run back along -axis, i.e. be
        // negative. Too short: push, so it must be positive.
        var impulse = separation <= 0.0 || error == 0.0
            ? 0.0
            : (error > 0.0 ? raw.Min(0.0) : raw.Max(0.0));
        return ReplacedAt(
            ReplacedAt(bodies, joint.BodyA.Value, ApplyImpulse(a, axis * -impulse, anchorA)),
            joint.BodyB.Value,
            ApplyImpulse(b, axis * impulse, anchorB));
    }
```

```plato
    // The two bodies after one visit to a ball-and-socket: its three axes solved in
    // turn, each seeing what the previous one wrote. The swing and twist limits the
    // type declares are NOT enforced — they are orientation constraints, and this
    // file solves only positional ones.
    SolveJoint(bodies: Array<SolverBody3D>, joint: BallSocketJoint, stiffness: Number,
        seconds: Number): Array<SolverBody3D>
    {
        var afterX = SolveBallSocketAxis(bodies, joint, Vector3D(1.0, 0.0, 0.0), stiffness, seconds);
        var afterY = SolveBallSocketAxis(afterX, joint, Vector3D(0.0, 1.0, 0.0), stiffness, seconds);
        return SolveBallSocketAxis(afterY, joint, Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), stiffness, seconds);
    }
```
